title: Scaling Optimization-Oriented Hypernetworks for Implicit Neural Representations
claim: Our method mirrors one optimization step, forward and backward, with attention modules over tokens, giving a single-pass parameter generator.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right; forward chain, backward block, ADD; color-coded legend strip
description: A single wide block diagram with a title banner on top and a legend strip at the bottom. On the left, a gray forward-chain box holds a CA block and three pink φ modules. They take parameter tokens ω_i^t (orange arrows) and output pseudo-activation tokens τ_i^t. A large central gray box holds the backward block. Blue ψ^τ modules and green ψ^ω modules produce Jacobian tokens J. A white inset holds the blue ψ^δ modules and a CA block, and passes the loss signals δ_i. Blue ψ^∇ modules then produce the gradient tokens ∇_ωi L. On the right, a tall ADD block with a λ^t step-size box outputs the updated ω_i^(t+1). A red line carries z_ζ across the top. The legend explains the Q/K/V color roles: pink, blue and green.
caption: One iterative module of the proposed hypernetwork $\mathcal{H}_\Omega$, illustrated for a three-layer MLP target INR ($L=3$); the construction extends to arbitrary $L$. At iteration $t$, the forward chain (left, modules $\phi_i$) produces the pseudo-activation tokens $\boldsymbol{\tau}_i^t$ from the parameter tokens $\boldsymbol{\omega}_i^{(t)}$, seeded by $\boldsymbol{\tau}_0^t$ from $z_\zeta$ through the Cross-Attention (CA) block. The backward block (right) realizes one chain-rule step at each layer: $\psi^{\boldsymbol{\tau}}_i$ and $\psi^{\boldsymbol{\omega}}_i$ produce the local Jacobian tokens $\boldsymbol{J}^{\boldsymbol{\tau},t}_{i-1}$ and $\boldsymbol{J}^{\boldsymbol{\omega},t}_i$, which $\psi^{\boldsymbol{\delta}}_{i-1}$ and $\psi^{\nabla}_i$ contract with $\boldsymbol{\delta}_i^t$ to produce the propagated loss-signal $\boldsymbol{\delta}_{i-1}^t$ and the parameter-gradient tokens $\nabla_{\boldsymbol{\omega}_i}\mathcal{L}$; the backward recursion is seeded by $\boldsymbol{\delta}_L^t$, formed from $\boldsymbol{\tau}_L^t$ and $z_\zeta$ via the concat-plus-CA module. The ADD block then applies the refinement with predicted step size and forwards to the next module.
abstract: We present a hypernetwork that generates the parameters of an implicit neural representation (INR) for a given signal in a single forward pass, without test-time optimization. Existing hypernetworks for this problem either ignore the chain-rule structure of the test-time optimization that produces an INR or, when they preserve it, instantiate the structure with MLPs whose parameter count grows quartically in target-network width. Our central contribution is to show that this parameter-count cost is structural to the MLP instantiation, not to the optimization-oriented principle of preserving chain-rule structure, and to resolve it by replacing the MLP body with attention. The resulting hypernetwork combines three design choices: an output-neuron-centric tokenization that aligns the token axis with each layer's output-neuron axis; an information-flow consistency rule that fixes the role of every cross-attention module from the representation its output should occupy; and a token-space iterative rollout that realizes the five quantities one optimization step on the target INR computes as five cross-attention modules with parameter count independent of target-network width. Across five 2D and 3D INR generation benchmarks, our method outperforms the state-of-the-art single-pass and optimization-oriented baselines; scales to target-network widths at which the MLP-based optimization-oriented paradigm exhausts GPU memory; and produces the highest result on NeRF generation without ground-truth INR weights supervision.
